messages:
pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT P-2026-482 triggered — kv-prefetch service high error rate (us-west1). Pager: alex.k. possible prefix cache corruption affecting correctness across a subset of tenants.

alex.k: I’m paged, on it. jumping into logs and metrics. tagging ana for SRE.

ana_notifier: alex.k acknowledged the pager.

ana_notifier: Escalation -> eng-oncall if not resolved in 5m.

ana_notifier: (auto) link: https://grafana.internal/alerts/P-2026-482

ana_notifier: recent spike: 502s from kv-prefetch proxy + elevated tail latency on text-gen routes.

ana_notifier: morphing: error signature looks like stale-key check + NPE on prefix lookup.

ana_notifier: sample log: ```ERROR kv_prefetch: prefix_lookup failed for tenant=acme-corp prefix=billing-123 code=KV_CORRUPT stack=...(truncated)```

ana_notifier: ana taking lead — oncall handoff to ana in 2m.

ana_notifier: ana joined the channel.

ana: pulling recent deploys and config rollouts. no infra deploys in last 30m. a config push to prefix-routing service landed ~23m ago. likely suspect.

sanjay: I see a config change that enabled aggressive prefix prefetch for new tenant cohorts. rolling that back now.

katy: Sanjay — please coordinate with opsbot before changing production routing. we need a mitigation plan first.

opsbot: runbook step 3: if prefix cache correctness issue -> set bypass policy for affected prefixes, reduce prefetch QPS, and apply temporary tenant quota cap.

ana: executing runbook. first mitigation: add temporary cache-bypass rule for suspect prefixes to prevent corrupted entries from being read. command: ```curl -X POST https://config-api.internal/v1/prefix-rules -d '{"rule":"prefix:billing-*", "action":"bypass_kv_cache", "expires":"15m"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'```

opsbot: config accepted. bypass rule applied to prefixes: billing-*, invoice-*, charge-* (scope: prod/us-west1).

alex.k: verifying — traffic to those prefixes now hits origin, requests 504s reduced but latency up ~60ms.

ana: second mitigation: rate-limit aggressive prefetchers. setting tenant prefetch qps soft-cap -> 5/s from 50/s for cohort tag=aggressive-prefetch.

opsbot: quota change posted: ```/admin/tenants/capacity?tag=aggressive-prefetch&prefetch_qps=5``` -> deployed across edge proxies.

sanjay: also disabling background prefetch jobs for the cohort to halt writes to prefix cache. command: ```PATCH /jobs/prefetch?cohort=aggressive-prefetch&enabled=false```

katy: I'm running a targeted traffic-shaping rule: route 100% of requests for affected tenants to primary origin with KV bypass; fallback model used for edge caching disabled. snippet: ```trafficctl split --route billing-* --to origin=100 --fallback=0```

cs-lead: CS note — we have 3 enterprise customers reporting failed invoice fetches in last 10m, CS team is contacting them. ETA on full mitigation?

ana: initial mitigations applied. errors dropped from 18% -> 3% in 6m. continuing to monitor for correctness regressions.

dmitri: quick correctness check: running sample queries across tenants that previously failed. comparing authoritative KV read vs proxied read. so far proxied reads with bypass are returning consistent results.

alex.k: we still see sporadic 500s from the prefetch pipeline; appears to be a downstream consistency check failing and triggering NPE. I'm throttling prefetch worker concurrency: ```kubectl scale deployment prefetch-workers --replicas=2```

opsbot: worker replicas scaled. concurrency reduced. backpressure applied to queue.

sanjay: I'm pushing a small hotfix to prefix-routing to hard-fail on malformed entries (avoid NPE) — will push to canary first. command: ```git cherry-pick hotfix/avoid-npe && ./deploy canary prefix-routing```

ana: good. canary looks healthy after 2 rounds. proceeding to deploy hotfix to prod in 2m.

opsbot: hotfix deploy to prod completed. metrics: 500s from prefetch pipeline dropped to near zero.

cs-lead: customer impact: 3 customers with visible errors, total affected ~200k API calls. CS has issued interim communications and offered rollback window.

katy: telemetry note: token-level cost went up ~8% during bypass window; informing finance.

ana: action summary so far: 1) applied prefix bypass for billing/invoice/charge prefixes for 15m (extended as needed), 2) reduced prefetch QPS for aggressive cohort, 3) disabled background prefetch jobs for cohort, 4) scaled down prefetch workers, 5) deployed hotfix to avoid NPE.

opsbot: monitoring policy: elevated alarms set for 30m; if error rate >5% reopen pager.

alex.k: oncall handoff to sanjay in 20m; sanjay please continue watch and own paging if it regresses.

sanjay: will watch, thanks. I'll follow up with a post-incident checklist and coordinate with eng-runtime for a root cause follow-up.

dmitri: postmortem owners: dmitri + ana. I'll start timeline and collect logs. assigning follow-ups: fix config validation to prevent corrupted prefix rules, add unit tests around prefix NPE, and add targeted canary for config pushes.

cs-lead: CS outreach: top 3 customers contacted, status page updated: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/P-2026-482.

katy: ops items for next 24h: 1) revert bypass once KV integrity verified, 2) ramp prefetch qps gradually with safety gates, 3) add rollback guard to config-api.

ana: mitigation has held for 35m with error rate stable ~2.5% and no new customer reports in 12m -> closing active pager. leaving thread open for postmortem notes.

eng-oncall: recorded. switching channel to #postmortems for follow-up.

sanjay: thanks everyone. notes: do not re-enable aggressive cohort prefetch until validation pipeline is improved.

dmitri: I'll pull logs and attach timeline by EOD. assigning owners in the postmortem doc.

alex.k: thanks — great coordination. :thumbsup:
